steps.text: In a large bowl, mix soy sauce, honey, distilled white vinegar, garlic powder, ground ginger, vegetable oil, green onions and black pepper. Place desired meat in marinade. Marinate in the refrigerator at least 4 hours before grilling.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef or Chicken Marinade
raw_recipe.description: This dark, rich marinade can be used with any type of beef or chicken. If you want it spicy, mix in the chopped hot peppers of your choice. Yummy!
raw_recipe.name: Beef or Chicken Marinade

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, mix soy sauce, honey, distilled white vinegar, garlic powder, ground ginger, vegetable oil, green onions and black pepper. Place desired meat in marinade. Marinate in the refrigerator at least 4 hours before grilling.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! I used this on chicken, but can't wait to try it on beef. I used olive oil instead of veg. oil and low sodium soy sauce. I also opted for minced garlic from the jar vs. garlic powder. I pounded the chicken down to tenderize and to thin them out a bit before marinating them all day. They soaked up most of the marinade. I think using honey actually made the green onions stick better and I had no trouble with anything burning on the grill. If you like this marinade, you'll love Unbelievable Chicken from this site. UPDATE: I marinated sirloin steak with this marinade for 6 hours with the same modifications and it came out great. This does work on beef or chicken!

I made the marinade slightly differently than above and it turned out AMAZING! I left out the ginger (I just don't care for it), substituted brown sugar for the honey, substituted minced onion for the chopped onion, substituted apple cider vinegar instead of white distilled, and substituted olive oil for vegetable oil (very minor changes all-in-all). I cut up chicken breast tenderloins into half-inch cubes and marinated for 7 hours. Then I put them in a baking dish and baked them at 350 for 20 minutes. They were perfect! This marinade is an absolute keeper. My boyfriend raved about how delicious the chicken was! There were absolutely no leftovers. :)

I am trying this marinade out on flank steak today. Before adding the meat, I tasted the marinade to see if it needed anything extra. It was great, but I ended up adding 2 tsp. of minced garlic (from a jar) and it was even better. Let's see how this turns out tonight. Will update as soon as I try it. Thanks soo much for the recipe.
UPDATE: i stir fried the meat with 1/2 yellow onion sliced and fresh mushrooms. I served it over brown rice and my family loved it. The meat had a great flavor!

Fantastic! I used it on skinless chicken breasts that I halved. I heeded the advice on too much soy, so I halfed the amount and switched it out with a sesame dressing I bought from Trader Joes. I also used fresh ginger, and a bit of sweet yellow onion that I pulverized in the food processor. Oil was 1/2 olive oil, 1/2 vegetable oil. Just great. Would also consider it for a salad dressing. Marinate as long as possible, up to a couple days. Five stars from me. Honey makes it.

Fabulous. I, like some others, used minced garlic instead of powdered, and instead of honey I used brown sugar and (real) maple syrup. I marinated for about 8 hours on beef Chuck and made skewers. I poured remaining marinade on finished skewers...Outstanding. Whole family loved it, will do again, thanks for the recipe.

this was really tasty. I didn't have any ginger or green onions (I used dried onions instead) and it was still really good. I think this is a pretty flexible marinade. I also broiled my chicken breast because the weather isn't grilling weather quite yet. I did it for about 15 minutes flipping the chicken after 5 minutes twice, and then about every minute after that. turned out moist and oh so tasty.

Take three small/medium size BONELESS chicken breasts and poke several holes THROUGH each piece BEFORE marinading. Other than using olive oil instead of vegetable oil, recipe instructions were followed. Overnight marinading. With this recipe, you can grill without worry of drying out meat--and get an awesome restaurant style juicy taste. Once off the grill and onto a serving dish, seal chicken in aluminium foil for 15-30 minutes. I serve chicken thinly sliced, with fettuccine Alfredo or makes great chicken sandwiches.

We really liked this, however, I felt like it needed less oil and probably also a little less honey. I was looking for a little healthier option, so will probably go with about 1/3 of the oil next time and maybe 2/3 of the honey.

My wife and I love this recipe. We find it easier to mix the marinade in the blender. We make shish kabobs with it (don't marinade the chicken as long as the beef) and pour the marinade over the onions (raost a little in the oven first) and red and yellow peppers.

Each time we make it people comment on the flavor and ask for the recipe - which I hand over, of course.

A winner.

Trevor from Nova Scotia

Hokay, so normally I am terrible at making chicken -- baking, grilling, stovetop, you name it and I've botched it. The chicken always turned out dry and flavorless...that is, until I tried this recipe. 

I followed pretty much every single step to a "t", except the part about oil -- I've been trying to cook/eat healthier (otherwise I would've hauled my lazy bum over to the school cafeteria), and cut down the oil to 1/2 cup.

In a spurt of wannabe cooking creativity, I used 1/4 cup olive oil and 1/4 cup *DARK SESAME OIL*. After marinating my 2 lbs of chicken overnight and panicking because I thought I overused the sesame oil and it was gonna set my oven on fire (thankfully, smoke point of sesame oil is decently high, despite it not intended for baking), the chicken turned out AMAZING. Now I have enough chicken for 7 more meals, though I'll probably regain my frosh 15 thanks to this recipe. 

FYI -- I had enough marinade to use on 3 lbs of skinless chicken breasts.

this was a nice simple marinade.. i left out the honey and added some sesame oil to make it more asian.. cut down the ginger to 1/2 tsp bc i didn't want it overpowering everything else.. i feel like i've made this before or maybe just something similar.. either way ty for the recipe

We used this to marinate boneless, skinless chicken thighs for grilled chicken burgers. They were delicious! We marinated them for about 4 1/2 hours. My husband kept saying, " That is a really good marinade. You need to save that recipe!" Saved to favorites.

This is a simple tasty marinade. You don’t need to leave your meat in it for hours. I poured some of the marinade into the pan I was cooking the chicken in then added my veggies. Turned out to be a great meal.

Oh, my, I don't know what's wrong with my palate, but I thought this was awful. The ginger overpowered any other flavor. Clearly I am in the minority, so you may want to try this out. Just taste it before you put it on your meat.

This was good! I marinaded beef and chicken in 2 different containers and both came out really good. The chicken in particular was particularly tender from sitting in the marinade. If you are looking for a non-Asian marinade, this is a good contender.
Have made twice now & enjoy it. Added some sesame oil & sriracha. Will probably cut back on the amount of oil.

Holy smokes, this is one amazing marinade!! When we were grilling this outside (after marinating), our neighbor across the street came over to ask what smelled so wonderful. He then asked if he could have a copy of the recipe! The combination of garlic and ginger in this recipe truly sets it apart from other marinades. It makes your grilled beef or chicken taste and smell like it came from a steakhouse. Not sure why this recipe doesn’t have 1,000 5 star reviews. We love it!!
my new fave added a dash of lemon
I made this as written, marinated it 4 hours with chicken thighs, and finished on the grill. Yum, Yum, Yum! 5 stars!
Excellent. My favourite go-to marinade.
